title: Affine sections of the base-change unit square
statement: Let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $g:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be scheme morphisms, with fibre-product projections $g_X:X'\to X$, $f':X'\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-fibre-product]. Use the derived functors, fixed affine sections, and canonical base-change map $\mathrm{BC}_E:Lg^*Rf_*E\to Rf'_*Lg_X^*E$ [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-derived-direct-image, def-pc-affine-global-hom-base-change-map, def-pc-derived-base-change-map]. Supply six comparisons t,b,z,d,v,r with identity-on-sections and right-derived-unit normalizations as in [lem-pc-affine-sections-composition-comparisons]. Supply s and c comparing $g_{X*};\Gamma_f$ with $\Gamma_{f'};\rho$ and $Rg_{X*};R\Gamma_f$ with $R\Gamma_{f'};D\rho$, respectively, where s acts identically on sections and c satisfies the derived-unit normalization in lean.statement. For every $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, writing $\Gamma_R=R\Gamma_{\mathrm{id}_R}$, $\Gamma_B=R\Gamma_{\mathrm{id}_B}$, and $Q=Rf_*E$, one has $\Gamma_R(\eta_g(Q));r_{Lg^*Q};D\rho(\Gamma_B(\mathrm{BC}_E);d_{Lg_X^*E})=b_E;R\Gamma_f(\eta_{g_X}(E));c_{Lg_X^*E}$. No quasi-coherence hypothesis is made and no morphism is asserted invertible.

proof.text: Expand BC_E by its canonical counit definition. Transpose under the adjunctions of g and g_X. The canonical pullback-composition comparisons identify the two paths around the square; naturality of the adjunction units and the triangle identities of f and f' cancel the counit/unit pairs. This yields the direct-image unit description of the same base-change map.

proof.text: Apply sections to that unit identity. On underived sheaves t,z,v,s act identically on sections and account for the R-action. The equations hb,hd,hr,hc identify their derived counterparts with these underived maps after composing with the right-derived units. Compute on K-injective resolutions and use the right-derived universal property to identify the composites on every derived object E. The resulting equality is the displayed unit square, without an extension isomorphism or an arbitrary m.
